analysis: What changed versus the 5:00 AM brief: the bounce held, it did not extend. The freshest futures snapshot (Longbridge, 11:46 UTC) is unchanged from the 5 AM read — S&P +0.87%, Nasdaq +1.93%, Dow +0.13% — with other wires showing a slightly softer picture (S&P +0.70-0.83%, Nasdaq +1.6-1.8%), so the rally is consolidating rather than accelerating into the open. The new inputs since 5 AM are mostly color around the two big stories: Michael Burry called Nvidia 'a great trade' short-term while warning its moat erodes over five years; Jensen Huang is back at work and apologized to senior management Monday (single-source), with the House reply still outstanding as of Tuesday afternoon and a fake statement attributed to his wife now debunked; Goldman became the first major bank to pencil in a March 2027 hike on top of the near-certain December one, while Goolsbee called October CPI 'alarming' and Philly's Paulson argued for gradualism. Bessent's 'de-risk, not decouple' remarks plus a direct US-China AI-incident channel and a Trump-Xi meeting next week in Shenzhen are a small positive for the China-exposed chip names. CoreWeave's detail — a $132.5B backlog, up 138% — is the strongest fundamental signal of the morning. Signal vs noise: the backlog and the chip-wide breadth are signal; Burry's trade call, the dispersion-trade warning and BofA's 2027 crowded-trade note are positioning color; the IRGC mine claim stays unverified even as the oil move itself is confirmed. The open's test is unchanged: whether the Nasdaq's near-2% lead survives a session with the bond market closed and no fresh Treasury signal.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures held the overnight bounce into the final hour before the open: as of 11:46 UTC (Longbridge), S&P 500 futures +0.87%, Nasdaq-100 futures +1.93%, Dow futures +0.13%. Other wires showed a slightly softer read (TradingView/Benzinga ~10:16 UTC: S&P +0.70%, Nasdaq +1.60%, Dow +0.18%; SPY $755.13, +0.69% premarket). Tuesday's close: S&P 500 7,520.93 (-0.38%), Nasdaq 25,065.88 (-0.74%), Dow 52,231.89 (-0.30%).
headlines.why_it_matters: The relief rally is consolidating rather than extending — the same futures levels as at 5 AM — so the open tests whether buyers defend the Nasdaq's near-2% lead with the bond market closed.

headlines.headline: CoreWeave (CRWV) Q3 detail: revenue $3.661B, +168% YoY and ahead of the $3.56B consensus; diluted loss per share $1.27, narrower than the $1.46 expected loss; total revenue backlog $132.5B, +138% YoY, with ~36% expected to be recognized within 24 months; full-year 2026 revenue guidance raised to $13.0-13.3B. Shares +12.9% premarket; Nebius +11%+, Iren ~+7%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A $132.5B backlog is the strongest fundamental signal of the morning — it underwrites the AI-capex demand story that the whole chip complex is trading on.

headlines.headline: Michael Burry called Nvidia 'a great trade' in the short term after its two-day slide, saying he does not intend to hold it long-term and expects its competitive advantage to weaken over the next five years; he said the CEO controversy should not cause significant damage to the business. NVDA +4.9% premarket (QuantPartners), after falling 4.27% Monday and 5.47% Tuesday.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source investor color, but it frames the bounce as a trade, not a re-rating — the stock is still governed by the House timeline, with the reply due today and the Nov 17 earnings print ahead.

headlines.headline: Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia's Santa Clara headquarters Monday and apologized to senior management at a closed-door meeting, per people familiar with the matter (Hongxing News via PANews); employees described the mood as low. As of Tuesday afternoon he had not answered the three House chairmen, whose deadline to accept the Nov 18 closed-door briefing or propose another date is today; Chairman Mast said he would 'absolutely' subpoena if there is no response. A purported public statement from his wife Lori Huang circulating on X was debunked as fake — she has made no public statement.
headlines.why_it_matters: The governance overhang is unresolved on the day the deadline falls, and the fake-statement episode shows how much unverified noise is circulating around the name — verify before trading the headlines.

headlines.headline: Goldman Sachs became the first major bank to extend its Fed hiking call past December, now expecting another 25bp hike in March 2027 (more likely than January) and a December dot plot signaling a third hike; Chicago Fed President Goolsbee called October CPI 'alarming, almost overheating,' while Philadelphia Fed President Paulson argued for a gradual pace and said skipping a hike is a pace adjustment, not a direction change. CME FedWatch: 100% probability of a December hike, 86.2% for 25bp.
headlines.why_it_matters: The rate path keeps lengthening — December is priced as certain and March is now in play — which is the headwind sitting underneath the whole equity bounce.

headlines.headline: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said at the National Committee on U.S.-China Relations gala that the US objective is to 'de-risk, not to decouple' from China, and that the two countries are establishing a direct channel to alert each other to serious incidents involving advanced AI ('super intelligence') models. President Trump and President Xi meet next week in Shenzhen, ahead of a fourth encounter in Miami. China agreed to import at least 25M metric tons of soybeans and 10M metric tons of coal over two years.
headlines.why_it_matters: Official confirmation of a softer China trade posture and an AI-incident hotline is a small positive for China-exposed chip names (Nvidia, AMD) that have been whipsawed by export-control headlines.

headlines.headline: Oil held its rebound: Brent $92.83 (+1.46%) and WTI $86.73 (+0.80%) premarket (Longbridge). The Washington Institute counted 37 vessels attacked in/around the Strait of Hormuz in October — the highest monthly total since the war began — and 10 so far in November; UKMTO confirmed a tanker struck northeast of Lima, Oman, on Tuesday. The IRGC Navy's claim that tankers hit naval mines remains unverified by AP. The EIA's Nov 10 outlook has Brent averaging $124 in October (highest monthly average since July 2022, inflation-adjusted) and ~$100 in Nov-Dec; API data showed US crude inventories up ~9M barrels in the week ended Nov 6.
headlines.why_it_matters: The supply-risk premium is rebuilding even as equities rally — and the mine detail inside the story is still single-source and unverified, so treat that part as fragile even though the price move and the UKMTO strike are confirmed.

headlines.headline: Megacaps mostly higher premarket (Finnhub, ~7:52 AM ET): TSLA +1.70% to $386.25, GOOG +1.1% to $288.11, META +0.8% to $646.65, MSFT +0.39% to $535.22, AMZN +0.2% to $271.30, AAPL -0.54% to $346.61. Intel +5% premarket and Broadcom +4.4% rode the chip bounce. Tesla reported Q3 FY2026 on Oct 21 (EPS $0.48, revenue $28.05B); Apple reported Q4 FY2026 on Nov 2 (EPS $2.10, revenue $114.48B); Microsoft reported Q1 FY2027 on Oct 28 (EPS $4.89, revenue $92.28B).
headlines.why_it_matters: Most megacaps are riding the futures bounce with Tesla strongest; Apple is the lone decliner, giving back a little of its recent strength.

headlines.headline: Firefly Aerospace (FLY) Q3 revenue $110.7M, +259% YoY, with backlog at a record $1.7B, but adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $69.5M from $46.3M a year ago and the non-GAAP loss per share was $0.45, better than the $0.60 expected. Shares +2.2% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: Record backlog with widening losses is the high-growth, high-burn trade in miniature — the market is rewarding the top line while pricing the cash burn more strictly.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news overnight. The fresh angle is crude: WTI $86.73 (+0.8%) and Brent $92.83 premarket after the Hormuz incidents, which steadies the energy backdrop. Carried forward: record Q3 reported Nov 3 (revenue $357.2M, +43% YoY vs ~$348.1M consensus; Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M; DCF coverage 1.67x; EPS $0.33, ~$0.03 beat), the $0.525 per-unit distribution paid Fri Nov 6, and full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M. RBC raised its price target to $31 from $30 (Nov 7). Management flagged cost pressure — monthly lubricant costs exited Q3 ~25% above first-half levels and diesel hit an all-time high in September.
